name_reason: Follows data_fd2_battle_<descriptor> convention; battle-domain FX scratch cell. Descriptor captures both roles (per-cast AOE FX count, and FX-queue idx / write cursor) and implies the scalar counter/index type. No Ghidra address residue (0x53EC4 not embedded). No domain ID to preserve. A rename would touch globals.h + every call site for no clarity gain.
purpose: Dual-purpose 32-bit battle scratch cell: per-cast AOE floating-FX entry counter, and the write cursor/index into the parallel floating-damage FX queues.
logic_summary: Reset to 0 by the spell/item-use dispatchers at cast start. Each damage-number / miss-indicator producer loads it (MOV EAX,[0x53EC4]) as the base index into the three parallel FX queues (sprite-id 0x53C6C, x-offset 0x53D34, target-char-idx 0x53DFC), writes a 4-entry batch (some sprite-id slots may be 0 for blank digits), then advances it by 4 (ADD dword [0x53EC4],4). After all AOE targets are processed it equals the total FX entry count; cure/inflict helpers gate the projectile-path animation on (!=0), and fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths consumes queues[0..idx-1] as its loop bound. Accessed exclusively as a full dword; used unsigned.
element_semantics: Single scalar (not an array): simultaneously the count of enqueued floating-FX entries for the current AOE cast and the next-free write index into the 3 parallel FX queue byte arrays. Advances +4 per producer batch.
comment_original_issue: Pre-existing src block was accurate but said producers 'write a batch of up to 4 entries'; the producer loops always write exactly 4 queue slots and advance the cursor by 4 ('up to 4' only fits the visible sprite-id slots, the remaining ones being 0).
notes: BSS zero-init scratch global at 0x53EC4 (memory all-zeros). Ghidra data plate was null/blank -> created a concise summary consistent with the src comment. Verified access width and instruction forms via disassembly of fd2_show_damage_number (read MOV EAX,[0x53ec4] @ 0x1e18e/0x1e1b2; advance ADD dword ptr [0x53ec4],4 @ 0x1e1d0; loop CMP EBX,0x4 -> exactly 4 entries). Mutable (many WRITE xrefs) -> is_const=false. No logic/type/declaration changes made (refine-only).
